text:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts for /v1/generate in us-west-2. error_rate 5xx = 12% (baseline 0.6%), p50 latency 220ms -> 1.1s, p95 3.6s. linked runbook: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/runtime-5xx. paging suspected. auto-escalation to #incidents.

ophelia: seeing the same on dashboards, large increase in kernel OOMs on model-runner nodes. logs show repeated `SIGSEGV` and `Killed` entries.

sanjay: tagging @maya (oncall) — are you able to grab the oncall?

maya (oncall): oncall here, taking it. first pass: is this across all models or a specific family?

liam: narrowed to model-family/corebert-13b quantized variant; errors spike after ~8k tokens. other families stable.

ophelia: stack traces attached in logs: ```
[model-runner-5] runtime: fatal error: unexpected signal during runtime execution
SIGSEGV: segmentation violation
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
 goroutine 4321 [running]:
  ...
```

infra-bot: metric: node-memory-pressure > 92% on pool inference-usw2-gpu-2. evictions observed: 7 in last 10m.

maya (oncall): ok root cause hypothesis: heavy KV cache growth + quantized kernel path causing page faults -> segfault/oom under memory pressure. immediate mitigation options?

sanjay: live mitigations we can run now: 1) route traffic away from affected nodes to warm pool, 2) scale up dedicated warm pool, 3) toggle fallback to fp16 kernels for this model, 4) reduce batch_size and max_tokens via gateway routing.

liam: I can flip kernel fallback for corebert-13b to use stable-fallback-2026 profile. command: ```redwoodctl model update corebert-13b --runtime-profile stable-fallback-2026``` should be fast but may increase per-token cost.

ophelia: while that runs, recommend reducing batching to avoid large prefix KV inflation. gateway patch: ```
PATCH /v1/routing/weights
{ "route": "corebert-13b@us-west-2", "max_batch_size": 4, "max_tokens": 2000 }
```

maya (oncall): do that now. also enable circuit-breaker -> return 503 quickly for long requests. we need to protect the gateway and customers.

incident-bot: ACTIONS_LOGGED: route change, model fallback toggle, node scale request. paging oncall -> ops-sre.

liam: model fallback command executed, reported rollout id rfid_78321. watching logs.

infra-bot: autoscaler request accepted: +4 g4dn nodes in pool inference-usw2-gpu-2 (requested by maya).

ophelia: logs after fallback flip: fewer segfaults, but still some OOM KILLs during long sequences. p95 latency improving.

sanjay: next step: pin model version to last-known-good (corebert-13b@v2026-04-12) to avoid noisy rollout variants. command: ```redwoodctl model pin corebert-13b v2026-04-12 --scope=us-west-2```

maya (oncall): pinned. also initiating customer impact assessment: which customers had >1% error rate increase in last 15m? ops-sre runbook query: ```
SELECT customer_id, error_pct FROM telemetry.api_errors
WHERE route LIKE '%corebert-13b%' AND timestamp > now() - interval '15 minutes'
ORDER BY error_pct DESC LIMIT 10;
```

ophelia: preliminary list: three PLG customers: cust-chi-202, cust-echo-77, cust-fin-04 showing >8% 5xx. outreach recommended.

liam: temporary mitigation for these customers: add per-customer fallback routing to older model or reduce concurrency per API key. example: ```
POST /v1/customers/cust-chi-202/overrides
{ "route": "corebert-13b@v2026-04-12", "max_concurrency": 2 }
```

maya (oncall): applied overrides for the 3 customers. ops: notify CSMs to reach out, include ETA for full mitigation.

incident-bot: NOTE: canary traffic shows 5xx drop to 1.2% behind fallback; cluster-wide still settling.

ophelia: additional observation: host-level swap/paging activity high on affected nodes. kernel logs show `Out of memory: Killed process` and `COMMIT_LIMIT` warnings. we should avoid swapping for inference nodes.

sanjay: immediate hard mitigation: cordon and drain two worst nodes, restart model-runner service after clearing /tmp KV shards. commands: ```
kubectl cordon node gpu-23
kubectl drain node gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
ssh gpu-23 'sudo systemctl restart model-runner && sudo rm -rf /var/tmp/kvcache/*'
```

liam: coordinated drain started. restart on gpu-23 complete, model-runner restarted. logs show workers reloading checkpoints, KV cache recovered smaller.

maya (oncall): who's on hand to follow up with deeper RCA? I want a post-incident ticket with timeline, root cause, and mitigation plan (disable huge prefix KV by default, add memory guard rails, improve autoscaler thresholds).

ophelia: I’ll own the RCA. initial remediation notes: - disable quantized-kernel-by-default for corebert family, - add per-model memory budget and eviction policy, - add synthetic load tests that exercise long-context sequences.

sanjay: add a short-term monitoring alert: trigger when node swap rate > 0.5 MB/s AND 5xx > 2% for same pool.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: active -> mitigating. summary so far: root cause suspected memory pressure + quantized kernel path -> segfaults/ooms -> elevated 5xx. mitigations applied: routing overrides, fallback kernels, node scaling, draining & restart. customer overrides applied for top 3 impacted.

maya (oncall): Handoff: I'll remain primary until 12:30 UTC then pass to ops-sre followup. @ophelia make the RCA ticket and link here. ops-sre, take on ongoing monitoring and customer comms after 12:30.

ophelia: RCA ticket created: https://tracker.redwood/INC-4972. I'll fill timeline and attach logs.

liam: final note: need to add model-level telemetry for KV size over time; current metrics are node-level only. will propose change in eng-telemetry backlog.

maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll close alerts when 5xx < 1% sustained for 30m and all pinned rollouts stable. leaving handoff note in #eng-oncall. :thumbsup:
